battle.name: 烏坦戰爭
battle.theater: 卡加梅河與坦尚尼亞北部邊境
battle.brief: 一九七八年十月，烏干達越過卡加梅河入侵坦尚尼亞，烏坦戰爭爆發；戰事集中於兩國邊境，後由坦尚尼亞反擊，迫使烏干達撤軍。惠氏步槍（Winchester Model 1873）於一八七三年正式列裝，屬重複使用的後膛步槍。

kit.name: 惠氏步槍
kit.history: 惠氏步槍屬美國陸軍制式武器體系中的個人步槍，採槍機閉鎖與金屬彈殼，可重複使用，並能讓步兵進行快速連續射擊。

countries: 主要交戰國是衣索比亞與索馬里，但雙方的軍事組合都不限於國家常備軍。衣索比亞方面包括軍委領導的中央軍，以及1977年形成政治與軍事聯盟的厄立比亞人民革命民主陣線；其核心部隊厄立比亞人民解放陣線在北部作戰，提格雷人民解放陣線則向哈勒與謝赫侯賽因方向展開。中央軍與各解放陣線保有不同指揮鏈，在對索馬里作戰時合作，卻始終互相防備。索馬里方面由索馬里國家軍與西索馬里解放陣線共同投入兵力；前者提供坦克、炮兵、飛機與後續部隊，後者提供山地作戰、游擊及沿線警戒。戰區涵蓋奧加登、巴萊、哈勒、謝赫侯賽因、戈代與迪雷道瓦。蘇聯曾向交戰雙方提供軍援，美國此前亦與索馬里維持軍事合作，但兩國都不是本場戰役中直接投入地面戰鬥的正式交戰國。
countriesEn: The principal belligerents were Ethiopia and Somalia, although neither side fought with its regular armed forces alone. Ethiopia fielded the central army under the Derg alongside the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front, whose political and military alliance took shape in 1977. Its principal components were the Eritrean People's Liberation Front operating in the north and the Tigray People's Liberation Front moving toward Harar and Sheikh Hussein. The central army and the liberation movements retained separate chains of command, cooperated against Somalia, and simultaneously guarded against one another. Somalia committed the Somali National Army together with the Western Somali Liberation Front. The regular army supplied tanks, artillery, aircraft, and follow-up formations, while the WSLF supplied mountain troops, local knowledge, reconnaissance, and control of forward positions. The theater covered the Ogaden, Bale, Harar, Sheikh Hussein, Gode, and Dire Dawa. The Soviet Union supplied military equipment to both governments, and the United States had previously maintained military ties with Somalia, but neither was a formal belligerent committing ground forces to this battlefield.
people: 孟吉斯圖・海勒・馬里亞姆以衣索比亞軍委主席及最高軍事負責人的身分，決定把中央軍、炮兵和航空兵集中到迪雷道瓦、哈勒與奧加登方向；他保住迪雷道瓦這座補給中心，容許游擊隊進入山區，再以火力與裝甲逐步奪回道路樞紐。索馬里總統西亞德・巴雷則把常備軍與西索馬里解放陣線組成混合攻勢，由奧加登和巴萊向西北推進，並在迪雷道瓦受挫後繼續投入裝甲與炮兵。阿卜杜拉西・阿卜杜拉西是西索馬里解放陣線的重要政治領袖，負責把地方武裝、索馬里軍官與後方補給接成一個作戰體系。厄立比亞人民解放陣線領袖伊薩亞斯・阿弗韋爾基在北部牽制索馬里後，將可用兵力轉向哈勒戰區；提格雷人民解放陣線的梅萊斯・澤納維也參與這次東進，負責與厄方中央軍協同。孟吉斯圖、西亞德及兩位解放陣線領袖的決策，決定了戰役由索方攻勢、雙方拉鋸轉為厄方反攻的走勢。
peopleEn: Mengistu Haile Mariam, chairman of the Derg and Ethiopia's senior military authority, concentrated the central army, artillery, and air force on the Dire Dawa, Harar, and Ogaden axes. He preserved Dire Dawa as a supply center, allowed irregular forces to enter the mountain country, and then used artillery and armor to retake the road junctions in stages. Somali president Siad Barre combined the regular army with the Western Somali Liberation Front in a hybrid offensive advancing northwest from the Ogaden and Bale, and continued to commit armor and artillery after the failure at Dire Dawa. Abdullahi Abdulkadir was an important political leader of the WSLF and helped connect local fighters, Somali officers, and rear-area logistics into a single operational system. Eritrean People's Liberation Front leader Isaias Afwerki drew forces away from the northern front and redirected them toward Harar. Tigray People's Liberation Front leader Meles Zenawi participated in that eastward movement and coordinated with the Ethiopian central army. Decisions by these five men shaped the transition from the initial Somali offensive through mutual exhaustion to the Ethiopian counterattack.
kits: 索馬里常備軍在奧加登作戰的主要裝備包括1944年列裝的T-34/85、1950年列裝的T-54、1955年列裝的T-55中型坦克，1962年列裝的PT-76輕型坦克，1965年列裝的BMP-1裝甲步兵車，以及BTR-60／BTR-70裝甲運輸車和BRDM-2裝甲偵察車；炮兵以122毫米D-30榴彈炮和BM-37 82毫米迫擊炮為主，另有152毫米D-1榴彈炮。索軍另有MiG-21MF戰鬥機、Su-7攻擊機與Mi-8運輸直升機。衣索比亞方面的核心裝備是T-62、T-54及T-55坦克，同樣配備BMP-1、BTR-60／BTR-70、BRDM-2、122毫米D-30、152毫米D-1和82毫米迫擊炮，並以北約制式名F-5A／F-5B輕型戰鬥機、MiG-21MF及Su-7執行對地支援。步兵使用AKM、PKM、DShK、RPG-7與Strela-2，厄方另大量使用1974年列裝的AK-74；反裝甲方面有ZU-23 23毫米高射炮。依車型不同，T-34/85使用85毫米炮彈，T-54／T-55使用100毫米炮彈，T-62使用122毫米炮彈；BMP-1配73毫米機炮，D-30使用122毫米榴彈。Ural-375與ZIL-131重型卡車承擔燃料、備件和彈藥輸送，索方主要由柏貝拉或摩加迪沙轉公路，厄方則利用阿薩布港及吉布提港至迪雷道瓦的鐵路。所有型號均在1978年以前列裝。
kitsEn: The Somali National Army's principal equipment in the Ogaden included the T-34/85 medium tank, introduced in 1944, the T-54 of 1950, the T-55 of 1955, the PT-76 light tank introduced in 1962, and the BMP-1 infantry fighting vehicle introduced in 1965. It also used BTR-60 and BTR-70 armored personnel carriers and BRDM-2 reconnaissance cars. Its artillery centered on 122 mm D-30 howitzers, BM-37 82 mm mortars, and 152 mm D-1 howitzers, while its air arm included MiG-21MF fighters, Su-7 attack aircraft, and Mi-8 transport helicopters. Ethiopia's core inventory consisted of T-62, T-54, and T-55 tanks, supplemented by BMP-1, BTR-60 and BTR-70, BRDM-2, 122 mm D-30, 152 mm D-1, and 82 mm mortars. Ethiopian F-5A and F-5B light fighters, MiG-21MF aircraft, and Su-7 aircraft provided ground support. Infantry on both sides carried AKM rifles, PKM and DShK machine guns, RPG-7 launchers, and Strela-2 man-portable air-defense systems, while Ethiopia also employed the AK-74 introduced in 1974. Anti-aircraft defenses included the ZU-23 23 mm cannon. Tank ammunition matched each vehicle: 85 mm for the T-34/85, 100 mm for the T-54 and T-55, and 122 mm for the T-62; the BMP-1 carried a 73 mm gun, and the D-30 fired 122 mm rounds. Ural-375 and ZIL-131 heavy trucks moved fuel, spare parts, and ammunition. Somalia drew on the ports of Berbera and Mogadishu before moving inland, while Ethiopia used Assab and the railway from Djibouti to Dire Dawa. Every model listed had entered service before 1978.
tactics: 第一階段始於1977年7月13日，西索馬里解放陣線從奧加登方向進入巴萊，索馬里常備軍則以坦克、炮兵和步兵沿主要公路向西北展開，目標是戈代、謝赫侯賽因與哈勒；解放陣線成員以RPG-7和輕重機槍攀越山脊、破壞側翼交通據點，常備軍則控制道路與車隊。第二階段在8月19日至20日前後的迪雷道瓦攻勢中達到高潮，索軍把裝甲部隊投入正面，遊擊隊分別攻擊城郊與高地，但攻擊梯隊因道路狹窄、彈藥消耗及側翼牽制而難以展開，厄方守軍保住了這座鐵路與公路樞紐，進攻者被迫撤回。第三階段是十月至十二月的拉鋸，厄軍由阿瓦什、阿夫德姆向戈代施壓，又從迪雷道瓦方向反攻哈勒；炮兵先摧毀暴露陣地，MiG-21MF與F-5A／B再攻擊集結車隊，裝甲部隊沿公路推進，解放陣線則依靠山脊與村寨據點逐段抵抗。第四階段在1978年1月至2月，厄方以T-62、T-55和D-30形成集中火力，先以航空兵打擊解放陣線陣地及道路補給，再由步兵清剿、以拖車和整備組配合裝甲前進，終於在2月上旬奪回戈代，切斷索軍通往巴萊的短距離補給線。第五階段由北部戰區發起，伊薩亞斯・阿弗韋爾基率厄立比亞人民解放陣線及梅萊斯・澤納維參與的提格雷部隊向哈勒與謝赫侯賽因施壓，迫使索軍分兵防守後方；索軍裝甲縱隊因油料、維修和道路牽制難以迅速集中，厄方聯軍遂在3月占領哈勒並向奧加登南部追擊。索馬里於3月19日宣布單方面停火，常備軍在月底前陸續撤出，解放陣線主力則向東部山區退縮。
tacticsEn: The first phase began on 13 July 1977. The Western Somali Liberation Front entered Bale from the Ogaden while the Somali National Army expanded northwest along the principal roads with tanks, artillery, and infantry. The WSLF used RPG-7 launchers and machine guns to cross ridges and threaten roadsides, while regular units guarded the avenues of approach and protected their supply columns. The second phase reached its climax around the attack on Dire Dawa on 19 and 20 August. Somali armor was committed to the frontal approach while irregular fighters struck the outskirts and heights, but the attack formations were unable to deploy fully because of the narrow approaches, ammunition expenditure, and demands on their flanks. The Ethiopian defenders retained this railway and road junction, and the attackers withdrew. From October through December, Ethiopian forces pressed from Awash and Afdem toward Gode and counterattacked toward Harar from Dire Dawa. Artillery opened the exposed positions, MiG-21MF and F-5A/B aircraft struck concentrations and road columns, and armor advanced along the highways while the WSLF resisted from ridges and fortified settlements. During January and February 1978, the Ethiopians concentrated T-62 and T-55 tanks with D-30 howitzers. Air attacks disrupted WSLF positions and replenishment roads, infantry reduced the fortified areas, and recovery crews and tractors supported the armor. Gode was retaken in early February, severing the short supply route toward Bale. The next phase came from the northern front. Isaias Afwerki's EPLF and the TPLF forces associated with Meles Zenawi pressed toward Harar and Sheikh Hussein, forcing Somalia to divide its forces to protect the rear. Somali armor columns could not concentrate quickly because of fuel, maintenance, and road constraints. By March, Ethiopian and liberation-front forces occupied Harar and pursued the attackers into the southern Ogaden. Somalia announced a unilateral ceasefire on 19 March, its regular forces withdrew during the following days, and the main WSLF formations withdrew into the eastern mountains.
data: 可核對的時間資料如下：索馬里與西索馬里解放陣線發動全面攻勢的日期是1977年7月13日；迪雷道瓦主要戰鬥集中於8月19日至20日；哈勒與謝赫侯賽因方向的激烈爭奪發生在同年十月至十二月；戈代於1978年2月上旬被厄方中央軍奪回；索馬里宣布停火並下令撤退的日期是3月19日。從7月13日至3月19日相隔249日，但零星交火與部分游擊行動延續至月底，因此249日只代表主要戰役及政治停火公告的跨度。地理上，前線由三個互相銜接的戰區組成：東南側為奧加登與巴萊，中部為戈代、謝赫侯賽因及哈勒，西北側為迪雷道瓦與阿夫德姆。主要補給線包括衣索比亞的阿迪斯阿貝巴—阿瓦什—阿夫德姆—戈代公路、阿薩布—戈代公路，以及吉布提港—迪雷道瓦鐵路；索馬里可由柏貝拉或摩加迪沙經公路向西南或西北展開。雙方先後投入的作戰人員均達數萬量級，厄方在1978年初可投入的坦克、炮兵和航空兵逐漸超過索方集中於巴萊的部隊。現有史料對陣亡、受傷、被俘及失聯的分項與總計常有不同口徑，因此不採用任何單一精確傷亡數字。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology is as follows: the full-scale offensive by Somalia and the Western Somali Liberation Front began on 13 July 1977; the principal fighting around Dire Dawa occurred on 19 and 20 August; intense competition for Harar and Sheikh Hussein ran through October and December of that year; Ethiopian central forces retook Gode in early February 1978; and Somalia announced the ceasefire and ordered withdrawal on 19 March. The interval from 13 July to 19 March was 249 days, although isolated clashes and some guerrilla activity continued until the end of March, making 249 days the span of the main campaign and the political ceasefire rather than every subsequent engagement. Geographically, the front comprised three connected sectors: the Ogaden and Bale in the southeast, Gode, Sheikh Hussein, and Harar in the center, and Dire Dawa and Afdem in the northwest. The principal supply routes were the Addis Ababa-Awash-Afdem-Gode road, the Assab-Gode road, and the railway from Djibouti to Dire Dawa. Somalia could move supplies inland from Berbera or Mogadishu by road. Both sides committed forces on a scale of tens of thousands, while the Ethiopian side gradually fielded more tanks, artillery, and aircraft in the Ogaden than Somalia had concentrated in Bale. Surviving accounts differ in how they count dead, wounded, captured, and missing personnel, so no single precise casualty total is used here.
cause: 烏坦（奧加登，Ogaden）戰爭不是單一零星邊界衝突，而是1974年衣索比亞政權更替後，兩國在奧加登、哈勒與巴萊一線長期對抗的全面爆發。1973年西索馬里解放陣線公開成軍後，衣索比亞一度向其提供武器與訓練；索馬里則支援厄立比亞人民解放陣線等反政府武裝，使邊境同時成為兩國代理戰的場所。1974年9月軍委推翻海爾・塞拉西後，厄方在1975年前後逐步停止公開援助西索馬里解放陣線，並加強奧加登的駐軍與道路控制；索馬里常備軍則在1974至1975年間進入巴萊和哈勒方向，利用解放陣線的前線力量迫使厄方後撤。邊境據點歸屬、軍援交換、政權安全及蘇聯和美國各自在此地的影響，使雙方互信迅速惡化。1977年7月，厄方在奧加登的兵力部署與西索馬里解放陣線的攻勢匯合，索馬里常備軍由東面及東南面加入，使原本由地方武裝主導的邊界戰爭轉為國家軍正面參與的區域戰役。
causeEn: The Ogaden War was not an isolated border incident but the full-scale eruption of a prolonged confrontation between Ethiopia and Somalia across the Ogaden, Harar, and Bale after the Ethiopian political upheaval of 1974. After the Western Somali Liberation Front became a public organization in 1973, Ethiopia initially provided it with weapons and training. Somalia simultaneously supported the Eritrean People's Liberation Front and other armed movements opposed to Addis Ababa, turning the frontier into a theater of proxy warfare. Following the Derg's overthrow of Haile Selassie in September 1974, Ethiopia gradually ended overt assistance to the WSLF around 1975 and strengthened its garrison and road control in the Ogaden. Somalia's regular army entered the Harar and Bale sectors during 1974 and 1975, using the WSLF's forward formations to force Ethiopian withdrawals. Disputes over border positions, the exchange of military assistance, regime security, and the respective influence of the Soviet Union and the United States rapidly destroyed confidence between the two governments. In July 1977, Ethiopian deployments in the Ogaden coincided with a renewed WSLF offensive. The Somali National Army then entered from the east and southeast, converting a conflict previously carried mainly by local armed groups into a regional war involving regular state forces.
impact: 作戰層面上，這場戰爭使衣索比亞重新取得奧加登西部、哈勒與巴萊交通線的主動權，西索馬里解放陣線的重型武器、補給車隊與前沿據點遭受重大損失，但該組織並未完全消失，仍在奧加登東部山區保持武裝存在。索馬里常備軍退回國內後，不再能以哈勒和戈代方向直接威脅衣索比亞的東部補給線；衣索比亞也因長期維持南方防線而更加依賴蘇聯的坦克、炮兵、飛機與維修體系，並把厄立比亞人民革命民主陣線各部視為必須安撫或壓制的政治力量。北部解放陣線則因作戰功績、繳獲裝備和軍事經驗獲得更高的政治地位，這些資源使其在隨後與軍委中央軍的衝突中更為有力，並在1991年進入阿迪斯阿貝巴、改變衣索比亞最高政治領導。索馬利亞在南方失去既有據點與軍事主動權後，更急於尋求美國及阿拉伯國家的資金與合作，而蘇聯的軍援重心也較偏向衣索比亞。
impactEn: Operationally, the war restored Ethiopian initiative in the western Ogaden and along the Harar and Bale approaches. The WSLF suffered heavy losses in artillery, motorized transport, and forward positions, although it did not disappear and retained an armed presence in the eastern Ogaden mountains. After the Somali National Army withdrew, it could no longer threaten Ethiopia's eastern supply routes directly through the Harar and Gode corridors. Maintaining the southern front also made Ethiopia more dependent on Soviet tanks, artillery, aircraft, spare parts, and maintenance, while the central government regarded the EPRDF components as political forces that had to be accommodated or restrained. The northern liberation movements gained military experience, captured equipment, and political standing from their role in the campaign. Those resources strengthened them in later confrontations with the Derg's central army and helped them enter Addis Ababa in 1991, changing Ethiopia's highest political leadership. After losing its southern positions and strategic initiative, Somalia sought funding and military cooperation more urgently from the United States and Arab states, while the Soviet Union's assistance tilted more heavily toward Ethiopia.
result: 到1978年3月底，衣索比亞中央軍與厄立比亞人民解放陣線聯軍已控制哈勒、謝赫侯賽因、戈代及巴萊的主要接近道路，索馬里常備軍撤回奧加登南部與本國境內，西索馬里解放陣線的主力則分散於東部山區，未能再以原有序列控制主要公路和城鎮。索馬里於3月19日宣布單方面停火，常備軍的撤收主要在月底完成；衣索比亞接受這一結果，但停火初期仍有零星戰鬥與局部陣地交涉。作戰結果是衣索比亞及其聯軍取得明確勝利，索軍在奧加登的攻勢、戈代與哈勒方向的補給及南部包圍全部失敗。戰役留下的局勢並未完全解決：西索馬里解放陣線仍具殘餘戰力，衣索比亞中央軍與北部解放陣線之間的權力矛盾也隨後擴大，使這場對索馬里的勝利立即轉化為衣索比亞內部權力格局改變的另一個起點。
resultEn: By the end of March 1978, the Ethiopian central army and the forces allied with the EPRDF controlled Harar, Sheikh Hussein, Gode, and the principal approaches to Bale. The Somali National Army withdrew into the southern Ogaden and then into Somalia, while the main WSLF formations dispersed into the eastern mountains and could no longer hold the principal highways and towns in their previous order. Somalia declared a unilateral ceasefire on 19 March, and the regular army's withdrawal was substantially completed by the end of the month. Ethiopia accepted that outcome, although isolated fighting and local arrangements over positions continued immediately after the announcement. The operational result was a clear Ethiopian and allied victory: the Somali offensive, its Gode and Harar supply lines, and its southern envelopment all failed. The war did not settle every underlying issue. The WSLF retained residual combat power, and the political conflict between Ethiopia's central army and the northern liberation movements widened afterward, turning the victory over Somalia into the starting point of a major redistribution of power within Ethiopia.
